system:
You are assembling a clinical visit note. The sentences of one note are listed below in random order with their section headings removed. File every sentence under one of these four headings: SUBJECTIVE, OBJECTIVE EXAM, OBJECTIVE RESULTS, ASSESSMENT AND PLAN. In the JSON, the headings are the keys subjective, objective_exam, objective_results and assessment_and_plan. Return each sentence ID under exactly one heading. Do not leave any sentence out and do not invent IDs.

SECTION DEFINITIONS
- SUBJECTIVE: what the patient reports and the history taken before the examination: the reason for the visit, the history of the present illness, the review of systems, past medical, surgical, family and social history, current medications and allergies.
- OBJECTIVE EXAM: what the clinician found on physical examination at this visit, including vital signs measured at the visit.
- OBJECTIVE RESULTS: results of laboratory tests, imaging and other studies that were reviewed.
- ASSESSMENT AND PLAN: the clinician's diagnoses or impressions, the reasoning behind them, treatment decisions, prescriptions, orders, referrals, patient instructions and follow-up.
A sentence goes under the heading that names its role in the note, not its topic. A symptom the patient reports belongs under SUBJECTIVE even if the plan discusses it again; a sentence that restates a symptom or finding to justify a decision belongs under ASSESSMENT AND PLAN.

For each sentence also give placement_confidence: HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW, meaning how sure you are that it belongs under that heading rather than another. If any sentence is LOW, set requires_review to true.

<sentences>
S1: CT scan of chest, obtained at an outside facility, is reviewed today and demonstrates a solitary 2 cm nodule in the lateral aspect of the right upper lobe.
S2: I explained to the patient that his procedure will consist of 3 small incisions being made on the side of his right chest.
S3: He notes that he enjoys biking.
S4: He denies any family history of lung cancer.
S5: I will then insert a camera and scope to assist in removing the nodule along with a very small portion of his lung.
S6: It could be a benign nodule, but because of his smoking history, I think it is best that he has it surgically removed.
S7: Nodule will be removed via video assisted thoracoscopy.
S8: - Auscultation of Lungs: Clear and equal bilaterally.
S9: He will have a chest tube in until the following day when I remove it at his bedside.
S10: Patient reports taking methotrexate 7.5 mg every week.
S11: No evidence of any type of emphysematous disease is present.
S12: Respiratory: Denies cough or shortness of breath.
S13: Right upper lobe lung nodule.
S14: Pulses are intact in all extremities.
S15: Patient reports his mother has a history of breast cancer, but is doing well.
S16: Mild swelling to the 3rd digit knuckles on the bilateral hands, consistent with RA.
S17: Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.
S18: He was advised that he will be admitted for most likely an overnight stay.
S19: No clicks, rubs, or murmurs.
S20: - Patient Education and Counseling: I encouraged the patient to continue to follow up with his rheumatologist.
S21: - Auscultation of Heart: Regular rate and rhythm.
S22: - Medical Treatment: Continue medication therapy and routine follow up with rheumatologist as previously outlined.
S23: PET CT will also be scheduled to determine if the nodule is metabolically active, which can suggest if it is cancerous or inflammatory.
S24: Patient reports he stopped smoking tobacco 7 years ago and has felt better since doing so.
S25: Surgery will require general anesthesia and will take approximately 1.5 hours.
S26: - Medical Reasoning: The patient has incidentally found right upper lobe lung nodule visible on his chest CT.
S27: He denies any previous history of lung infections or pneumonia.
S28: Capillary refill is brisk.
S29: Patient reports a history of rheumatoid arthritis.
S30: - Medical Reasoning: Stable.
S31: Rheumatoid arthritis.
S32: - Examination: Skin is pink, warm, and dry.
S33: - Patient Education and Counseling: I had a thorough discussion with the patient concerning surgical treatment.
S34: All questions were answered.
S35: - Examination: No lower extremity edema.
S36: It appears the nodule is smooth in appearance.
S37: - Medical Treatment: Pulmonary function test ordered today to obtain patient's baseline.
</sentences>
